sanjay: Heads-up — onboarding opt-13b-quant today. Found a tokenizer quirk where escaped angle brackets like \u003c\u003e are tokenized separately and shift the chat template offsets. Anyone run into this with the new HF-derived tokenizer?

lina: Hmm, not that exact escape. Is this at encode time or when we reserialize to tokenizer.json?

sanjay: At encode time. Example: prompt has '<user>hi</user>' and tokens insert extra tokens for '\u003c' and '\u003e' instead of mapping to the special tokens in the chat template.

matt: Could be special_tokens_map mismatch. Quick check: does tokenizer.json have "special_tokens" or a "add_tokens" entry for the literal '<user>'?

michelle: Also check if the tokenizer was trained with byte-level processing vs normal. Byte-level can split weird escapes.

lina: Can you paste a minimal repro (input -> token ids) ?

sanjay: Yep, did a small run:
```python
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
t = Tokenizer.from_file("/models/opt-13b-quant/tokenizer.json")
print(t.encode("<user>hi</user>").tokens)
print(t.encode("<user>hi</user>").ids)
```
Output: tokens show ['\\u003c', 'user', '\\u003e', 'hi', '\\u003c', '/user', '\\u003e'] which is wrong for our chatfmt that expects ['<user>', 'hi', '</user>'].

matt: Ok that explains the offset. Two quick paths: 1) map the escape sequences back to real chars in pretokenize step, or 2) add the literal strings as special tokens so they are single tokens.

ops-bot: Reminder: weights for this build are staged at s3://redwood-models/onboarding/opt-13b-quant/2026-03-15/. Do not overwrite production bucket.

michelle: I'd prefer adding special_tokens for chat markers so downstream code doesn't need pre-normalization. But we should audit other models for conflicting token ids.

lina: I can run a quick scan across the model catalog for malformed escape tokenization. Script:
```bash
python scripts/check_tokenizer_specials.py --dir models/ --patterns '<user>' '</user>' '<assistant>'
```
Returns a small list where tokenizer.split_on_escape == True.

sanjay: Good call. If we add special tokens, what's the process to update tokenizer.json safely for Dedicated/Private? Need to keep compatibility with existing checkpoints.

matt: Add to tokenizer as add_special_tokens -> update tokenizer.json and release a minor patch to model metadata. For serving: rollout via canary config in console (route to opt-13b-quant:v2 for 10% traffic) and fallback to opt-13b-quant:v1 on mismatch.

michelle: Also add a config lint rule to catch escape-literal splits. Something like: check that all chat markers resolve to single token id when encoded. If not, fail validation.

lina: I'll open a tiny PR that adds the lint and a migration script that injects the 3 markers. PR will include test that verifies tokenization for a set of sample prompts.

sanjay: Sweet. For bookkeeping: please add the weights path to the onboarding checklist and note the tokenizer.json hash so we can trace release.

ops-bot: Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ONB-412 (tokenizer escape handling).

matt: Quick snippet for the migration (for the runbook):
```python
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
from pathlib import Path
p = Path('/staging/opt-13b-quant/tokenizer.json')
t = Tokenizer.from_file(str(p))
new = ['<user>', '</user>', '<assistant>']
for s in new:
    if t.token_to_id(s) is None:
        t.add_tokens([s])
        # ensure saved as special
        t.save(str(p))
```
Note: we prefer add_special_tokens on the Transformers wrapper, but this shows the idea.

michelle: Good. Lina — can you also add a short note in the onboarding runbook about preferring normalization step over token injection when dealing with escape-heavy datasets? Some customers may rely on literal escapes.

lina: Will do. I'll make the PR and ping here for review. ETA: EOD my timezone. :eyes: 

sanjay: Thanks all. Once PR merges I'll trigger a canary and run the chat-template regression suite.

michelle: If CI flaps, tag me. Otherwise we'll promote to v2 afterward.

sanjay: Closing the loop here. Added note to ONB-412 with tokenizer.json sha256 and weights path. Thanks!
